summary: Kimi Desktop is a thin Electron shell over the CLI daemon and exposes NO UI/view/theme extension surface — the UI-customization goal is unachievable via the supported plugin API and should not be re-investigated. Real extension points are skills (shipping), mcpServers (highest unclaimed value), sessionStart, and the unproven hooks/systemPrompt. All manifest fields are emitted by scripts/install-kimi-desktop-plugin.sh; the only kimi.plugin.json in-repo belongs to liter-llm, so changes edit the GENERATOR, never a manifest file.
open_questions: Is ~/.local/bin on the daimon's PATH, or are absolute paths accepted in mcpServers? change-kde-001 is blocked until this is answered.
Do the desktop daimon honour `hooks` and `systemPrompt`? Both are documented for the CLI plugin path and absent from all 12 vendor packages.
Is there a catalog/description budget at 145 skills, as Codex has at ~360?
review_warnings: PATH prerequisite for change-kde-001 is stated but not yet resolved — plan must not schedule 001 before it is.
The 7 MCP server names are asserted from session knowledge, not evidenced in the review packet; verify each is a real launchable server before emitting it.
kbd-status was confirmed present by directory listing, but its suitability as a sessionStart payload is unverified.
skillInstructions is already used by the pack but carries no explicit adopt/reject rationale in the extension-point list.
